title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. X is a topos and k a coefficient ring. u: Z -> P (written \U0001D513 in the notes) is what Grothendieck calls an 'immersion'. The relation mu = lambda + Theta with Theta u = 0 shows that the maps are additive. So most likely Z is the constant sheaf Z_X (drawn with a double stroke), and P is a flat abelian sheaf (or k-module) containing it, with u a monomorphism.

Objects. Put Phi = P_k and Psi = (P/Z)_k, with d: Phi -> Psi the projection. Then L = Ker d is the image of Z, which is free of rank 1 (case g of the next page, 'trivialisé'). Let K_{u,k} = Gamma^*Phi (x) Lambda^*Psi be the 'algèbre de De Rham à p.d. élémentaire' (next page). It is bigraded by:
- exterior degree j;
- weight i, with Gamma^i (x) Lambda^j sitting in total degree i+j.
It carries a PD structure and a differential raising the exterior degree, extended as a PD-derivation.

Resolution. In weight n the complex 0 -> Gamma^n L -> Gamma^n Phi -> Gamma^{n-1}Phi (x) Psi -> ... -> Lambda^n Psi -> 0 is exact. This is the Koszul resolution of a divided power of the kernel of a surjection of flat modules. So K_{u,k} resolves Gamma^*L = k{T}, the divided power polynomial algebra.

Theorem (previous page) and its relative form (this page). For f: X -> Y there is a natural map f_*K_{u,k} -> Rf_*(k{T}) = Rf_*(k) (x)_Z Z{T}.
- It is an isomorphism in each bidegree (i,j) with j <= i (j = cohomological degree, i = weight).
- The left side is zero, hence its differential is zero, for j > i, since Gamma^i (x) Lambda^j = 0 there.
Equivalently, in weight i, f_*K^{i,*} is quasi-isomorphic to the truncation tau_{<= i} Rf_*(k).T^{[i]}. This is what 'isomorphisme avec un certain tronqué du second' means.

What this needs. The iso cannot hold for arbitrary P. It requires the terms Gamma^a Phi (x) Lambda^b Psi with b < i (all with a >= 1) to be f_*-acyclic, presumably a hypothesis on P made on earlier pages. Granting that, dimension shifting gives the iso for j < i. At j = i it also holds, since H^i(L) = coker(Gamma(C_{i-1}) -> Gamma(Lambda^i Psi)).

Functoriality.
(a) In k: clear.
(b) In u: given a second immersion u': Z -> P' and lambda: P -> P' with lambda u = u', lambda induces a PD-algebra map lambda-bar: K_u -> K_{u'}. It is compatible with all structures and covers the identity on k{T}, so it is a quasi-isomorphism. It stays an isomorphism after applying Gamma(X,-) or f_*, since both sides compute the same truncation.

Independence of the choice. If mu also satisfies mu u = u', write mu = lambda + Theta with Theta u = 0. Then Theta factors through Psi = P/Z, giving Theta: Psi -> Phi'. The evident continuation is to use Theta as a contraction, exponentiated via divided powers, to build a homotopy between lambda-bar and mu-bar. This is the standard embedding-independence argument familiar from crystalline cohomology, here in a linear toy model. The page breaks off at 'on trouve Theta u = 0'.

Purpose. To give a functorial, multiplicative (PD-algebra) cochain model computing the truncated cohomology H^{<= i}(X,k).T^{[i]}, assembled into a bigraded PD algebra over k{T}. It is a 'divided power de Rham complex' attached to an embedding of Z (or of a rank 1 module) into a nice sheaf, independent of the embedding up to canonical homotopy.
errors: The isomorphism f_*K -> Rf_*(k){T} in bidegrees j <= i cannot hold for an arbitrary monomorphism Z -> P. It needs f_*-acyclicity of Gamma^a(P_k) (x) Lambda^b((P/Z)_k) for b < i, presumably assumed earlier but not restated here.
'La dif. du premier membre est nulle pour j>i' is trivially true: the first member is zero for j>i, since Gamma^i (x) Lambda^j = 0 when j>i (as stated on the next page).
The independence-of-choice argument (mu = lambda + Theta) is left unfinished on this page; no homotopy is written down.

ideas.what: Koszul-type complex Gamma^*Phi (x) Lambda^*Psi resolving the divided powers Gamma^*L of the kernel L of a surjection Phi -> Psi of flat modules
ideas.modern_name: Koszul complex / divided-power Koszul resolution (Gamma^n L -> Gamma^{n-j}Phi (x) Lambda^j Psi)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent I, ch. I §4), Akin–Buchsbaum–Weyman (1982)

ideas.what: f_* of the bigraded resolution computes the truncation tau_{<= i} Rf_*(k).T^{[i]} weight by weight, packaged as a bigraded PD algebra over k{T}
ideas.modern_name: acyclic resolution computing truncated derived pushforward; cochain-level divided-power algebra model

ideas.what: Functoriality in the embedding u and independence of the choice of lambda up to homotopy, via Theta = mu - lambda vanishing on Z
ideas.modern_name: independence of embedding via PD homotopy (as in crystalline cohomology)

missed.claim: The homotopy between lambda-bar and mu-bar for two choices of lambda is not constructed on this page. The thread stops at Theta u = 0.
missed.quote: alors, posant μ=λ+Θ, on trouve Θu=0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of minor interest; the expected argument (PD-exponential of a contraction) is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine functoriality and truncation bookkeeping for a divided-power Koszul resolution. It gives some insight into the content of the little-documented 1976 IHES talk, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: The subscript in K^{··}_{u,h} and \bar\lambda_h is most likely k (the coefficient ring), i.e. K^{··}_{u,k}, \bar\lambda_k, consistent with the previous page.
The second immersion is written u': ℤ -> 𝔓' (with a double-struck/stroked Z, probably the constant sheaf ℤ), not u: Z -> 𝔓'.
'qui est un isom. dans ladite catégorie dérivée' — the manuscript reads roughly 'dans telle catégorie dérivée' (any relevant derived category); the meaning is unchanged.
